faq.a: Malaika is associated with the Arabic form مَلَائِكَة, whose core sense is malaika; angels.

faq.q: What is the origin of Malaika?
faq.a: Malaika is associated with Arabic. Malaika is Arabic مَلَائِكَة (Malāʾika), the plural of مَلَك, meaning 'angels'.
Yes — the underlying form مَلَائِكَة is Arabic.
Malaika can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Malaika should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root م ل ك is Quranic, but Malāʾika is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Malaika mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Malaika is rendered ملائکہ and carries the sense ملائکہ، فرشتے.

faq.q: What does Malaika mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Malaika is rendered ملائکه and carries the sense ملائکه، فرشتگان.
A romanized syllable approximation is ma-lai-ka. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Malaika?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Malaika, malaika. Script forms are ملائکه, ملائکہ, مَلَائِكَة, मलाइका.

faq.q: Is Malaika a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
